slot.brief: Compare energy of an electron in a given orbit of a hydrogen-like ion with the corresponding orbit in hydrogen; ask for the ratio in terms of Z and n.

stem: For a hydrogen-like ion of nuclear charge $+Ze$, what is $E_n(\text{ion})/E_n(\text{H})$ for electrons in the same orbit $n$?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV; for H, E_n = -13.6/n² eV. The ratio is Z².

working:
$E_n(\text{ion})=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\ \text{eV}$; $E_n(\text{H})=-13.6\dfrac{1}{n^2}\ \text{eV}$.\n$\dfrac{E_n(\text{ion})}{E_n(\text{H})}=Z^2$.

Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV; for H, E_n = -13.6/n² eV. The ratio is Z².
solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $E_n=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$, while for hydrogen, $E_n=-13.6\dfrac{1}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$.
$$\frac{E_n(\text{ion})}{E_n(\text{H})}=Z^2$$
